segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 79: The Literature Club’s Pen Pal

In the end, the results of the class committee election were that Li Luo and Hua Xiuxiu were still the class president and vice president.

The two sports representatives also remained unchanged.

Shi Yanran, who ranked second in the class on the opening exam, was elected as the Youth League Secretary, while Xu Yinghuan, relying on her sweet and lovely voice, successfully secured the position of academic representative.

Jin Yuting didn't participate in the election, but she had already volunteered to be the English class representative during English class before.

As for Shao Heqi, he didn't even go up this time.

He figured he couldn't compete with Li Luo, and since he couldn't be class president, he certainly wasn't going to be another class committee member, working under Li Luo.

After the class committee election ended, the first self-study period was over.

Yan Zhusheng looked at his name written on the blackboard, with the title of sports representative above it, and couldn't help but sigh.

"Why didn't any girls run for sports representative?"

"Why didn't any brave souls run for class president?" Li Luo also voiced a soul-searching question.

Yan Zhusheng glanced at him, stopped thinking about it, and asked instead, "After school today, are we going straight to my place?"

"I have to attend the Literature Club's welcome party at noon," Li Luo said. "After it's over, we can go to your place together and buy some groceries on the way."

"Okay." Yan Zhusheng thought for a moment. "Then I'll go check out the Rock Club at noon."

"Is the Rock Club fun?"

"It's alright," Yan Zhusheng commented seriously. "Everything's fine except for the fact that it's not very professional."

"They're high school students, don't have such high expectations." Speaking of which, Li Luo suddenly asked curiously, "If you join the Rock Club, what position would you play in the band? Keyboard? Guitarist? Or lead vocalist?"

"I can do any of them," Yan Zhusheng said. "I can also play the drums. It depends on the arrangement."

"Sounds pretty interesting."

"Then why didn't you join before?"

"Mostly because I found it troublesome..."

The Rock Club had few members.

After all, in a school like No. 1 Affiliated High School, most of the students were good students who paid more attention to their grades than anything else.

Activities like being in a band, which have a relatively high barrier to entry, could dissuade a bunch of people right from the start.

Not to mention, the instrument most people learned was likely the piano; guitarists, bassists, and drummers were pitifully few.

Plus, the twelfth graders would quit the club every year, so the actual band was only composed of tenth and eleventh graders.

Therefore, the Rock Club was one of the few small clubs in the school, with its numbers consistently remaining under ten people.

It was already good if they could gather one person for each position to practice songs.

"Well, you can come and check it out when you're interested," Yan Zhusheng said. "Sometimes we're short on people, you can come be a guest player."

"That could work."

Soon, the bell for the second self-study period rang.

Li Luo started doing his homework, occasionally picking up his scratchpad to chat a little with Yan Zhusheng.

The morning passed by quickly.

At noon, Li Luo called Yan Zhusheng, and after waiting for Ying Chanxi to come downstairs, they headed to the cafeteria together.

They met up with Xu Youyu on the way. The four of them had lunch in the cafeteria and agreed to meet at the school gate later.

Afterward, Yan Zhusheng went to the Rock Club, while Li Luo and the other two walked toward the Literature Club's classroom.

The club president, Duan Qintian, had finished his meal early and rushed to the classroom, instructing the eleventh-grade members to do some simple decorations.

By a little after twelve noon, most of the members had arrived.

Li Luo sat in a corner with Ying Chanxi, boredly spinning the ballpoint pen in his hand.

After a series of simple self-introductions, President Duan Qintian explained the rules and requirements of the Literature Club, and finally, they entered the pen pal interaction session.

This was what Xu Youyu had mentioned to him before, that members of the Literature Club could correspond with each other through letters.

The premise was that both people agreed.

Duan Qintian took a stack of envelopes from Qin Yawei's hand, placed it on the lectern, and said with a smile, "Now, everyone can try writing a letter, then put it in an envelope and give it to the pen pal you want to get to know here."

"The pen pal who receives the letter can choose to reply or not in the following days."

"And state in the letter whether you're willing to become the other person's pen pal and continue corresponding."

"We've prepared plenty of envelopes today, so feel free to write a few letters."

This was the first time Ying Chanxi had heard of this. When Xu Youyu mentioned pen pals to Li Luo, she was still in the bathroom taking a shower.

At this moment, her eyes lit up, and she turned her head to look at Li Luo. "This seems pretty interesting, huh?"

"Who are you going to write to?" Li Luo took the stationery Duan Qintian handed out, twirled the ballpoint pen in his hand, and asked with a smile.

Ying Chanxi shot him a look, then huffed, "I'm writing to my senior sister."

"Oh." Li Luo nodded and also started writing. "I'm writing to my senior sister too."

Ying Chanxi: "?"

Exasperated, Ying Chanxi secretly stomped on Li Luo's foot under the table.

Li Luo looked at her, speechless. "Aren't you childish? Why are you stepping on me?"

"I just want to. It's none of your business." Ying Chanxi pouted, lowered her head, and started writing her letter, ignoring him.

Soon, the only sound in the classroom was the rustling of pens on paper.

Li Luo wrote two letters, went up to the lectern to get two envelopes, sealed them, and then leaned back in his chair, scanning the room.

Among them, Hua Xiuxiu and Lin Yuan were sitting in another corner, seeming to be writing quite seriously.

As for the other club members, besides Xu Youyu and the other two presidents and vice presidents, Li Luo wasn't familiar with any of them.

He had only memorized their names during the self-introductions earlier.

Few people from the honors classes joined the Literature Club; it seemed they all chose the competition clubs.

Usually, after choosing a competition club, a person would likely pick an interest-based club as well. They certainly wouldn't be like Ying Chanxi, coming to the Literature Club just for the fun of it.

"Sigh..." Li Luo placed the two envelopes on the table and sighed helplessly. "If I hadn't promised my senior sister, I'd be tearing it up on the basketball court right now."

"So you feel wronged coming here with me, is that it?" Ying Chanxi had just finished one letter and was writing a second. Hearing his words, she immediately turned her head and glared at him.

"You're writing two letters?" Li Luo glanced over and asked at once, "One for your senior sister, and who's the other one for?"

"It's not for you, anyway," Ying Chanxi huffed, then asked, "Didn't you write two as well? One for your senior sister, and who's the other one for?"

"It's for you."

"Ah? Hmm... Oh... Is that so..." Li Luo's words immediately threw Ying Chanxi off her rhythm.

She had thought Li Luo would imitate her and say, "It's not for you, anyway."

She didn't expect Li Luo to be so direct. He left Ying Chanxi stammering, suddenly as if she'd forgotten how to speak, her heart thumping a little wildly.

"At least you know what's good for you," Ying Chanxi muttered under her breath and continued to write with her head down, though it was now bowed a little lower than before.

(End of this chapter)
